# Pin the range field's value-in-label display

## Welcome 👋

`Neo.form.field.Range` is a slider. With `showResultInLabel: true` it writes its current value in front of the label, `[40] Volume`, and keeps it updated as the slider moves. Small, visible behaviour, and no test. A friendly first spec.

This is a **good first issue** for Hacktoberfest 2026. It needs Node.js and a clone of this repository: no Docker, no AI setup.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Reserved for first-time Neo.mjs contributors.** The maintainer team will not claim, edit, or implement this issue through **2026-10-31**. Comment here to claim it, and ask anything on this issue.

**Set up once:** follow [Set up the engine from a clone](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#set-up-the-engine-from-a-clone), including `npm run bundle-browser-deps`: without it the unit suite selects zero tests.

## Where things live

- Source: `src/form/field/Range.mjs`. `getLabelEl()` and `getInputEl()` return the label's and the input's virtual-DOM nodes.
- New test file: `test/playwright/unit/form/field/Range.spec.mjs`
- Pattern to copy: `test/playwright/unit/form/field/InputWidth.spec.mjs` (creating a field in a unit test)
- Tip: `Range` extends the number field, which needs one main-thread stub while your tests run. Install it in `test.beforeAll`, only if it is missing, and remove it in `test.afterAll`, exactly as `test/playwright/unit/apps/colors/ViewportController.spec.mjs` does in its `test.beforeAll`: `const main = Neo.ns('Neo.main', true); if (!main.DomEvents) { main.DomEvents = {registerDisabledInputChars() {}, unregisterDisabledInputChars() {}}; /* delete it again in afterAll */ }`. Do not put it at the top of the file: another spec imports the real `DomEvents`, and `npm run test-unit` then stops with `Namespace collision in unitTestMode for Neo.main.DomEvents`.

## What to cover

| Case | Expected |
|---|---|
| `labelText: 'Volume'`, `showResultInLabel: true`, `value: 40` | the label text is `'[40] Volume'` |
| then `value = 60` | the label text is `'[60] Volume'` |
| `showResultInLabel` not set | the label text is just the `labelText` |
| any range field | the input's `type` is `'range'`, and its class list is exactly `['neo-rangefield-input']` |
| defaults | `clearable` and `useSpinButtons` are `false` |

## Done when

- [ ] `test/playwright/unit/form/field/Range.spec.mjs` exists, following the pattern file's setup.
- [ ] One `test(...)` per table row.
- [ ] Test-only: if the field disagrees with a row, say so on this issue before changing `src/`.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/form/field/Range.spec.mjs` passes.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit` passes.

## Out of scope

`tickmarks`, the `useInputEvent` DOM listener, and styling.

## While you wait for review

You just pinned one small piece of a multi-threaded application engine: in Neo.mjs your app's code runs inside a web worker, and the main thread only paints. Two things worth ten minutes:

- **See the part nobody expects.** Run `npm run build-themes -- -n -e dev -t all` and `npm run server-start`, open `apps/workstation/`, and drag a tab out of the browser window. It becomes its own OS window, still running, with the same component instances and the same worker. [Benefits: Introduction](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/benefits/Introduction.md) explains why that is possible.
- **Your coding agent can go much further here.** The skills this repository's AI maintainers work with are published on npm as [`neo-agent-skills`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/neo-agent-skills), and they need no Knowledge Base and no Memory Core. With Claude or GPT beside you, the `help wanted` issues are within reach after this one.
